summary: Researched the evening before (Wed 18 Nov); lineups and starting goalies are not out, so this is a draft until the morning check and the final check. Thursday has EuroLeague Round 13 (the second game of a double week for every team), Swedish SHL and KHL hockey. Every kept game needs a second price that agrees with Polymarket. Eight games were researched; two are medium. Medium: Valencia v Virtus Bologna (Valencia 9-3 and first, at home; Kalshi 80-83% agrees with Polymarket 82%; Mirotic and Reuvers likely out, third game in five days), Fenerbahce at Olimpia Milano (Fenerbahce 3rd at 8-4 against 2-10 Milano; Kalshi agrees at about 64-65%; Melli, Key and Bitim out, which explains the price easing from 70% to 66.5%). Low: Bayern v Baskonia (Bayern themselves 3-9, three players missing on Tuesday, no traded second price), Växjö v Björklöven ($13 market, no second price, coach sacked 1 Nov), Djurgården v Skellefteå, Färjestad v Frölunda and Brynäs v Luleå (starting goalies unknown, no clean second price). Excluded: Metallurg v Traktor (the 'Ural derby'). Tennis needs high confidence and was not researched. Morning check (Thu): Valencia stay medium (injury report unchanged, Kalshi 82-83%). Fenerbahce drop to low: their price fell another 4.5% overnight (0.665 to 0.635) with no news (Melli and Key were already known). Four games added this morning: Al Ain v Al Dhafra medium (3rd v 12th, Bovada about 90%), Peñarol v Cerro Largo medium (a win secures the annual table; Kalshi agrees at 67-68%; Peñarol winless in six, mostly draws), Al Wasl v Hatta low (no team news, unlabelled second price), Tappara v Vaasan Sport low (2 wins in 10, goalies unknown). Two more games checked to lift the odds: City Torque at Progreso low (price fell 6% in 24h with no news, no team news), Straubing at Krefeld low (no second price, goalie problems). The slip stays below 1.70 because no other game reached medium. Midday: three more games checked to lift the slip out of the closest tier: Maldonado at Boston River low (price fell 5.7% with no news), Zverev v Fils low (tennis needs high; Zverev already through, Elo 64%), Al Ahli v Al-Shamal low (models make it a coin flip, no second price). No other game reached medium, so the slip stays at about 1.68. Final check (17:52-18:45 UTC): Peñarol stay medium (price up to 69.5%, Kalshi and DraftKings agree; the official XI was not published by 18:45 UTC, a draw is the main risk). Valencia stay medium (Reuvers confirmed out, Mirotic game-time, price 81.5%, Kalshi agreed this morning).

games.reason: Valencia (9-3) at home vs 15th-placed Virtus (5-7). The afternoon injury report confirms Reuvers out, Mirotic is game-time and Mari uncertain, and Virtus are missing only Casarin. Live Polymarket is 0.805, down 1.5 points from first listing (-1.8%, under the 3% threshold) and 3 points from this morning, with no news beyond the already-expected absences. I put p at 0.78, below the market, because the frontcourt is thin (Reuvers out, Mirotic and Mari unconfirmed), it is Valencia's third game in five days, and there is no official lineup, no fresh Kalshi price and no bookmaker line. Confidence stays medium.
games.main_risk: Valencia's thin frontcourt (Reuvers out, Mirotic game-time, Mari uncertain) plus fatigue from a 3-games-in-5-days stretch with the Belgrade trip. Virtus come off an upset win over Panathinaikos. The market is thin and the price has been drifting down, so a further move or a bad official lineup would warrant dropping the leg.

checks.team_news: No new injury reported for Zverev or Fils (tennisuptodate, 19 Nov). Fils's 2026 season was disrupted by an earlier back injury, but he is back to near his best (beat Jodar 4-6 6-2 6-2 after losing to Shelton 6-2 3-6 6-3). No withdrawal or walkover announced.
checks.lineups: Order of play for Thu 19 Nov at Inalpi Arena, as reported by ATP daily schedule and Tennis Tonic: afternoon (14:00 local) Shelton vs Jodar, evening (20:30 local = 19:30 UTC) Zverev vs Fils. One stale schedule snippet listed Zverev vs Shelton in that slot, which conflicts; I read it as a stale listing. Not seen on the official ATP page directly.
checks.rotation: Zverev played Sun (Jodar) and Tue (Shelton), so Thursday is his third match in five days. Fils played Sun (Shelton) and Tue (Jodar). Both on equal rest. The semis are Sat 21 Nov.
checks.motivation: Zverev has already qualified for the semis (2-0: 6-4 6-4 over Jodar, 6-2 7-6(4) over Shelton). Per tennisuptodate he takes first place in the group if he wins one set against Fils, so his remaining aim is top spot. Fils (1-1) needs a result: he qualifies if he beats Zverev and Jodar beats Shelton. He also qualifies if he beats Zverev in straight sets and Shelton beats Jodar. Even if he loses in three sets to Zverev, he qualifies if Jodar beats Shelton. Shelton's and Jodar's match is played first, so Fils will know what he needs. Borderline on the hard rule 'favourite already qualified while the opponent needs the result'. I did not exclude because Zverev's group win is not yet secured, but it is the main risk.
checks.form: Zverev is 2-0 in the group without dropping a set, 25-16 in games. Fils is 1-1, 27-25 in games, and went to three sets in both matches. Tennis Abstract overall Elo is Zverev 2089.6 and Fils 1992.9. Hard Elo is 2030.1 against 1934.
checks.h2h: Zverev leads 5-2 over eight listed meetings at tour level (tennisuptodate/StatSniper). Fils won at least some of the recent ones. Indian Wells 2026 pre-match line was Zverev -165 and Fils +146. Fils's power game is a style risk in a fast indoor hard court, and he has taken sets off Zverev before.

Second price: Kalshi KXATPMATCH-26NOV17ZVEFIL (ticker date says 17 Nov, which looks odd for a 19 Nov match, so only partly reliable): Zverev yes 0.71 bid / 0.72 ask, Fils 0.28 bid / 0.29 ask, de-vigged about 0.71 / 0.29. This agrees with Polymarket within 2 points. No bookmaker moneyline found (data.odds absent from the candidates file). An older Zverev vs Shelton line was -201 at this event.

Win probability for Zverev is 0.636 overall and 0.635 hard, about 6 points below the market. StringTension Elo says 80.8% for Zverev but the page's date is unclear.

games.reason: Tennis legs need high confidence, and this one cannot get it. Zverev is already through to the semis and Fils has to win. The Elo model gives Zverev only 0.636 against 0.695-0.71 in the market. The Kalshi second price agrees with the market but its ticker date is doubtful and I found no bookmaker line. p is lowered to 0.67 to reflect the Elo gap and the motivation asymmetry.
games.main_risk: Zverev already qualified for the semis with a 2-0 record while Fils must win to stay alive. Fils also has a big-serve, big-hitting style that has taken sets off Zverev, and Zverev has less reason to push hard once top spot is secured by winning a single set (borderline hard-rule case).

No bookmaker moneyline found.

games.reason: Fenerbahce are still the better side on table and net rating (3rd vs 19th, +6.9 vs -6.2), won the last three meetings, and Kalshi (0.63/0.64) agrees with Polymarket (0.635). But the favourite's price has fallen 4.5% since first listing (0.665 to 0.635) and 3.0 points since last night, and no news this morning explains it: the Melli/Key absences were already known at listing, and no new Fenerbahce absence or Milano return was found. Under the brief's rule that is a low. I shade p to 0.61, 2.5 points below the live market, because of the thinner frontcourt, the double week with travel and the reported three straight away defeats.
games.main_risk: Unexplained price drift: the market has moved against Fenerbahce by 3 points since last night and 4.5% since listing with no public reason, which may mean information I did not find (a late fitness doubt, e.g. around Larkin or the guards, or a sharp bookmaker move). On court, a Fenerbahce side missing Melli and Key on a Tuesday-Thursday double week with travel can lose a close game away to a Milano side that is desperate and just ended a nine-game losing streak. No confirmed lineups yet.

Both sides are mid-to-lower table with no clinched position, so neither has 'nothing to play for'. No hard-exclusion case. The table is from a secondary source, not shl.se.

Before Malmö they had won 1 of 8 away games, and they had conceded 47 goals in 14 SHL games (about 3.3 per game) while having a 25.7% power play. Björklöven: lost 4-1 at Brynäs (14 Nov); last 10 games with goals not found. Earlier meeting: Björklöven won 4-2 at Växjö on 1 Oct 2026. Växjö's form is shaky and the coaching change is recent.

checks.odds: No second price found for this game: Svenska Spel, bet365, Hurbra and similar sites had no preview for 19 Nov, and the candidates file has no data.odds. Polymarket Växjö 0.765 / Björklöven 0.235. Volume is only about $13 and liquidity about $1,779, so the market is extremely thin. The 24h move was 0.760 to 0.765 (+0.7%), which is no concern. The market resolves on the final score including overtime and shootouts; the shootout winner counts as +1 goal. Without an independent price that agrees within about 5 points, the rule gives 'low'.
checks.models: No bookmaker-free rating found (no data.rating for hockey). Table only: Växjö 21 pts vs Björklöven 17 pts after 16 games each, a 4-point gap, which does not support a 76% favourite. Växjö's 3.3 goals conceded per game is weak.
checks.venue_weather: Home game for Växjö; Vida Arena in Växjö (indoor) was not independently confirmed. Polymarket lists the game for Thu 19 Nov, 1:00 PM ET (18:00 UTC), and Hurbra confirms Thu 19 Nov at home vs Björklöven. No neutral-venue signs.

games.reason: The fixture is verified and no hard exclusion applies. The coach change at Växjö was 17 days ago, so it is soft. Both sides are mid-to-lower table, so neither has nothing to play for. The market is a thin $13 with no independent second price, and the starting goalies are unknown. Växjö are only 9th, have a leaky defence and a new coaching setup, and lost at home 2-4 to this opponent on 1 Oct. The table gap does not justify 76%, so p is trimmed to about 70%. Confidence is low because of the missing second price and goalies.
games.main_risk: Växjö (9th, 3.3 goals against per game, caretaker coaches since 1 Nov, only 1 win in 8 away games before Malmö) lose to a Björklöven side that already beat them 4-2 this season. A backup goalie, or a one-goal OT/SO game, is also possible. The Polymarket price is untested at $13 volume.

Rated low because the starting goalies are unconfirmed on both sides (Hellberg illness flag for Djurgården), Skellefteå is on short rest after Tuesday's CHL game plus a long trip, Djurgården is unbeaten at Hovet this season, the Polymarket market is thin, and no clean de-vigged two-way second price was found. p is lowered by 4 points from the market.

Goalie status is unknown for both teams.
